items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: So the day he died, he told my sister, says, 'Aunt Daisy, I thought I could beat this, but I can't beat it.'

ctx.x: Yeah, just started to decline. So the day he died, he told my sister, says, 'Aunt Daisy, I thought I could beat this, but I can't beat it.' He says, 'But I don't want you all to worry because I've accepted it.' He said, 'It was very hard,' says, 'I hate to leave my little boys.

They won't even know they had a dad," he says, "but that's what's worrying me more than anything else. But don't you all worry," he says, "because I'm ready." And didn't even go in a coma, just closed his eyes and died. So that kind of got to me, you know, it really shook me up. And I guess when I went over there, there was so many -- some of those -- you know, sometimes I would start at the festival like at 12:00 and maybe do one show and the festival would go like to 12:00, you know, at night, from 12 to 12,…
